text:
Samir Patel: Heads up — we're seeing interface flaps and rising RX errors on a subset of p5dn hosts in us-west-2. Affects clusters: infer-prod-1 (AZ a/c) and training-gpu-2. Application-level errors from east-west RPCs. Anyone digging in?

Leila Chen: Yep, alerted earlier. Latency spikes between pods in the same AZ, packet loss ~5-12% reported by the app. I saw repeated ifdown/ifup for eth0 on two hosts.

Maria Gomez: Pasted key logs from one host (p5dn-uw2-02):
```
[ 1234567.890123] mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: NIC: link port 1 state changed to DOWN
[ 1234567.890456] eth0: Rx errors: 2541, Tx errors: 0, dropped: 312
[ 1234568.001234] mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: firmware event: port flapping detected
```
and ethtool -S shows:```
rx_errors: 2541
rx_missed_errors: 312
tx_errors: 0
mlx5_core_port_up_events: 42
```

Kevin O'Neill: Interesting — RDMA stack also logged a few events: `rdma: mlx5: port 1 flapped, clearing qp state`. So the problem is hitting both kernel netdev and rdma layer.

Leila Chen: MTU differences? We had a config drift last week when we rolled kernel patches. On these hosts eth0 MTU is still 1500, but other nodes moved to 9000 for jumbo frames. Could be jumbo/fragmentation mismatch.

Samir Patel: I ran a quick iperf3 test between two affected hosts: 11% packet loss on UDP with 8972 payload, TCP sessions stall intermittently. iperf3 log: `sender dropped 9.8%`

Maria Gomez: Repro steps I used:
- ssh to p5dn-uw2-02
- sudo ethtool -k eth0
- sudo iperf3 -c p5dn-uw2-03 -u -b 5G -l 8972 -t 30
- watch dmesg for mlx5 entries

infra-bot: Automated alert: 3 hosts in infer-prod-1 marked degraded due to netdev errors. Runbook link: https://intra.redwood/ops/netdev-flaps

ops-oncall: Can we isolate to firmware/driver? Driver version: `mlx5_core v5.13-rc`, firmware reported `FW 20.30.1020` on these nodes. Vendor recommends FW 21.x for p5dn variants.

Kevin O'Neill: We should not mass reboot in prod without rollback plan. Suggested immediate mitigation: 1) drain affected nodes, 2) shift inference shards to other AZs, 3) open ticket with vendor (Mellanox/AWS NIC team) for firmware guidance.

Leila Chen: I've started draining p5dn-uw2-02 and p5dn-uw2-04. Marked them `unschedulable`. Scaling is tight — moving traffic will spike our cross-AZ egress and incur cost. FYI estimated additional infra cost if we keep failover for 6 hours: ~$1.2k.

Samir Patel: Can we try forcing MTU 9000 on the affected hosts temporarily to see if flapping reduces (to test fragmentation hypothesis)? If that stabilizes, it points to a path-MTU/driver bug.

Maria Gomez: Did that on one host in staging earlier — setting MTU 9000 dropped Rx errors from ~400 to ~8 within 10 minutes, but that's staging and a single host. Also saw fewer rdma qp resets.

infra-bot: Note: changing MTU in prod will break any non-jumbo endpoints in the same L2. Confirm during maintenance window.

ops-oncall: Next steps I propose: A) coordinate vendor ticket with logs (dmesg + ethtool -S + firmware ver), B) schedule small maintenance window to update NIC firmware on a canary host in prod (p5dn-uw2-02 after drain), C) monitor rdma/eth counters for 30m post-update, D) rollback plan to reimage if fw update fails.

Kevin O'Neill: I'll open the vendor ticket and include `tcpdump`/pcap from a flap event. @Maria can you collate pcap + dmesg for the three hosts and attach to ticket?

Maria Gomez: On it. I'll attach: dmesg, /var/log/messages snippet, `ethtool -S` output, `rdma stats`, and a 60s pcap captured during the next flap (using `tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/flap.pcap -c 100000`).

Samir Patel: Also adding a graph to the console: per-host `eth.rx_errors` and `rdma.qp_resets` to track progress. If we see errors drop consistently after FW uptick, we can roll.

Leila Chen: FYI — we had an older kernel bump last week that changed mlx5 driver behavior. If vendor says firmware won't fix, we'll need to pin kernel or revert. Keep that in mind for scheduling.

ops-oncall: For immediate customer-facing risk: routing policy updated to prefer eu-west and us-east for latency-sensitive inference for next 4 hours. This prevents hot-path failures while we remediate.

Kevin O'Neill: Ticket opened with vendor: INC-38192. Included logs and link to this thread. Will update with vendor feedback.

Samir Patel: Thanks. Please ping #all-hands if vendor asks for larger outage. I'll keep monitoring and update here when canary fw update completes. :thumbsup:

Leila Chen: Thanks all — keeping this thread as single source. I'll update drain/unschedule list in the runbook.

infra-bot: Maintenance action recorded: hosts drained: [p5dn-uw2-02, p5dn-uw2-04].

Kevin O'Neill: Signing off for now, will re-check after vendor reply.

Maria Gomez: Uploaded artifacts to INC-38192.

Samir Patel: Canary firmware update scheduled in 15m (non-disruptive mode). Will report results here.
